continuity_scope: Tomi Adeyemi, Children of Blood and Bone, Henry Holt and Company (BYR) first US edition, 6 March 2018, ISBN 9781250170989, 448 pages. This is the first Legacy of Orïsha novel only. Later novels, any film/adaptation material, interviews, classroom commentary, and claims about real traditions are outside story canon.

coverage_rule: Include the four named viewpoint protagonists Zélie, Tzain, Amari, and Inan; the named monarch King Saran; Zélie's named mentor Mama Agba; named resistance/magic exemplar Lekan; named regime commander Kaea; and Amari's named friend Binta, whose death materially begins Amari's break with the court. This nine-person cohort covers every viewpoint, the monarch and commander pursuing them, the training/revival figures, and the named precipitating palace victim. Other named divîners, maji, soldiers, nobles, villagers, animals, spirits, deities, clans, and institutions are omitted.
omissions: Children of Virtue and Vengeance, Children of Anguish and Anarchy, all future or companion work, film/adaptation material, interviews, teaching guides, and translations as independent continuity evidence.
Named but non-cohort maji, divîners, kosidán, soldiers, royals, villagers, rebels, spirits, animals, and incidental historical figures.
Orïsha, maji/divîners/kosidán, clans, titles, ashê, deities, magic, the Raid, the scroll, majacite, animals, places, and royal/military institutions as character nodes.
uncertainties: The novel changes viewpoint among Zélie, Amari, Inan, and Tzain. Claims identify a viewpoint where it materially limits knowledge, motive, or interpretation.

Its West African/Yoruba-inspired fantasy vocabulary is fictional source material. Orïshan terms, deities, clan labels, and spell-like language are not evidence about Yorùbá religion/culture or any other living tradition, and no direct equivalence is asserted.
Diacritics follow the source where available (for example Orïsha, divîner, ashê, ikú, èmí, and Ìmólè). Search/display editions vary; unaccented forms are aliases or search variants, never new terms.

The novel depicts institutional persecution racialization/colorism, class hierarchy, genocide/collective trauma, murder, torture, imprisonment, family violence, war, grief, and hostile romance. Records are non-graphic and do not reduce identities to oppression.

The Macmillan US page’s current excerpt includes later-series text, which is not used. The UK excerpt's copyright/map/clan pages and Chapter One are only opening-witness evidence; all later-book claims remain excluded.
